data.title: TCS-Bosch Deal Could Shift Up To 3,000 Employees From Captive Technology Operations
data.description:
The exploratory discussions could give TCS access to engineering teams while helping Bosch evaluate its technology operations and cost structure

Tata Consultancy Services (TCS) is in early discussions to acquire part of Bosch’s technology and product development operations in India, in a potential transaction that could involve the transfer of up to 3,000 employees, according to a report by Mint.

The proposed deal remains at an exploratory stage, with discussions expected to move to the board level next month before any decision is taken. The scope of the operations involved, the number of employees who may move and the final terms of the transaction have not been determined.

The potential acquisition comes as Bosch evaluates options to reduce costs by transferring some of its technology and product development activities. For TCS, the transaction could strengthen its engineering capabilities and provide access to specialised talent working on emerging technologies, including physical artificial intelligence (AI).

Bosch Evaluates Technology Operations

According to the Mint report, Bosch is considering the sale of a part of its India-based technology and product development operations as part of its cost-containment efforts.

The proposed transaction could give TCS access to engineering teams involved in technology development and product engineering. The opportunity comes amid growing interest in physical AI, which involves integrating artificial intelligence into machines and physical systems, including robotics and autonomous vehicles.However, the discussions remain preliminary, and neither the scope of the proposed transfer nor the employee movement has been finalised.

Bosch’s India Technology Footprint

Bosch established its Indian technology operations in Bengaluru in 1997 through Bosch Global Software Technologies (BGSW). Over the years, it expanded its presence to Hyderabad, Pune and Coimbatore.According to the report, India accounts for approximately four-fifths of Bosch’s global Global Capability Centre (GCC) workforce, which stands at around 28,900 employees.

Bengaluru accounts for approximately half of this workforce, while the remaining employees are based across the company's other Indian locations.The proposed transaction relates to Bosch's technology and product development operations and is separate from the business of listed Bosch Ltd, the Indian automotive components manufacturer.

Robert Bosch GmbH is the majority shareholder in Bosch Ltd through its promoter group companies. However, according to the report, Bosch Ltd does not directly oversee the GCC operations involved in the discussions.

TCS Expands Technology Capabilities

The potential transaction would add to TCS's recent acquisitions and strategic engagements involving captive technology and consulting operations. The IT services company has pursued such deals to strengthen its technology capabilities, expand its talent base and deepen relationships with global clients.In October, TCS acquired Best Buy's India technology centre. In August, it acquired Porsche's management and IT consulting arm, MHP, in a transaction valued at US$373 million. The company also secured a five-year IT modernisation contract with Porsche valued at US$1.45 billion.

The proposed Bosch transaction would follow a broader trend of multinational companies transferring captive technology centres to IT services providers. Such arrangements can provide service providers with access to established engineering teams and long-term service contracts, while allowing multinational companies to reassess their operating costs.

However, the transfer of employees from captive centres can also create initial margin pressures for acquiring IT services companies, particularly where existing salary structures are higher.Sushovon Nayak, Lead IT Analyst at Anand Rathi Institutional Equities, told Mint that long-term service contracts can help IT companies secure revenue over several years amid uncertain demand conditions.

Board Discussions To Determine Next Steps

The discussions between Bosch and TCS reflect the changing approach of multinational companies towards their captive technology operations, as IT services providers seek specialised engineering capabilities and more predictable revenue streams.The proposed transaction is still at an early stage, with board-level deliberations expected next month. The number of employees involved, the specific operations under consideration and the commercial terms remain uncertain.

If finalised, the deal could represent a significant movement of engineering talent from a multinational company's captive technology operations to an IT services provider in India's technology sector.

data.title: Karnataka Bank Names Udaya Kumar Hebbar MD And CEO
data.description:
The banking veteran takes on a three-year term, bringing experience across commercial banking, rural finance and microfinance

Karnataka Bank has appointed Udaya Kumar Hebbar as its Managing Director and Chief Executive Officer (MD and CEO) for a three-year term, following approval from the Reserve Bank of India (RBI). The approval was communicated through a letter dated 16 November 2026. The bank will inform the stock exchanges of the date on which Hebbar assumes charge.

Hebbar brings more than four decades of experience across banking, financial services, credit operations and rural finance. He previously served as Managing Director and CEO of CreditAccess Grameen from September 2010 to June 2025, leading the microfinance lender through a period of business expansion, an initial public offering (IPO) and subsequent capital raising.

Career Across Banking

Hebbar began his banking career at Corporation Bank in 1985, working across branch management, clearing and credit operations. He joined ICICI Bank in 1995, where his responsibilities included corporate credit, payment operations, centralised operations, quality initiatives, rural and micro banking, and agricultural business.

In 2007, he joined Barclays India as Head of Commercial and Payment Operations. His experience across banking operations, credit and rural financial services has shaped a career spanning traditional banking and financial inclusion.

Leadership At CreditAccess

Hebbar joined CreditAccess Grameen as Chief Executive Officer in 2010 and became its Managing Director and CEO in 2015. During his tenure, the company expanded its operations and customer base, with assets growing from Rs 250 cr in March 2011 to around Rs 26,000 cr by March 2025, according to his professional profile.

The lender also expanded its reach to more than 2,000 branches across 16 states and one Union Territory, serving over 4.8 million micro-borrowers as of March 2025. Hebbar led the company through its IPO in 2018 and a qualified institutional placement (QIP) in October 2020.

He retired from his executive role in June 2025 and continued as a Non-Executive Director on the company’s board.

Board And Leadership Roles

Hebbar currently holds non-executive positions across financial services and related organisations. These include Non-Executive Director roles at CreditAccess Grameen and CreditAccess Life Insurance, Non-Executive Chairman of CreditAccess India Foundation, and Deputy Chairperson of the Supervisory Board at CreditAccess India B.V.

A commerce graduate and postgraduate in commerce, Hebbar is also an Associate of the Indian Institute of Bankers (CAIIB). His leadership development includes programmes at Harvard Business School, INSEAD, IMD, London Business School and IESE.

Priorities At Karnataka Bank

Hebbar’s appointment brings experience in commercial banking, operational management and financial inclusion to Karnataka Bank’s leadership. His three-year term begins when he formally assumes charge, with the bank set to notify the stock exchanges of the effective date.

data.title: Cities Need More Than Buildings
data.description:
Dr Sanjeev Vidyarthi, Provost, Anant National University, on the need to rethink design education to address urbanisation, climate resilience and India's evolving cityscapes

India's rapid urbanisation and evolving environmental challenges call for a broader approach to design education, one that connects architecture with urban planning, technology, sustainability and social responsibility. In an email interaction with BW Education, Dr Sanjeev Vidyarthi, Provost, Anant National University, discusses the need for interdisciplinary curricula, industry-academia collaboration and responsible use of artificial intelligence (AI) to prepare graduates for real-world challenges. Edited excerpts:

How can Indian design education move beyond conventional architecture training to address urbanisation, climate resilience and the complex challenges facing Indian cities?

Design and architecture education in India have notable strengths such as rigorous training and the impartation of a disciplined work ethic. However, translating imaginative studio work into practical solutions that address the complex challenges of rapid urbanisation, ongoing climate change and sustainable development remains an important task.

As India pursues the ideal of Viksit Bharat, architecture and design education needs to move beyond designing individual buildings and isolated institutional campuses towards a comprehensive understanding of cities, their communities and the relationship between people and their environment. This requires curricula integrating sustainability, technological innovations, contextual knowledge and interdisciplinary learning, while drawing upon India's regional diversity, traditional wisdom and Indigenous Knowledge Systems.

Understanding cities also requires recognising the interdependence of their physical infrastructure, natural environment, economic activities and social systems. Design interventions need to respond to these relationships rather than trying to address individual problems in isolation.

Ultimately, the objective is to prepare technologically adept and socially empathetic, responsible professionals with a broad understanding of complex situations they seek to address. Closer alignment between educational institutions, industry and policy frameworks will further strengthen their ability to shape built environments that are ecologically responsible, culturally responsive and economically resilient for the decades ahead.

What changes are needed in higher education curricula to bridge the gap between design theory, interdisciplinary learning and the practical demands of urban development?

Much of the India we envision for 2047 is currently being built and young professionals are already shaping the way India develops into Viksit Bharat. It is therefore essential to purposefully rethink and restructure higher education to nurture appropriately skilled professionals who can identify and address the diverse demands of our rapidly changing urban world.

To enable this change, higher education in India needs to break traditional disciplinary silos and take a more interdisciplinary pedagogical approach. HEIs must offer a more dynamic academic environment to students complemented by immersive learning experiences, community engagements, industry collaborations and regular opportunities to work on real-world problems.

They must also create stronger connections between classroom learning, studio work and professional practice. Students should have opportunities to test ideas, evaluate their feasibility and understand the practical constraints involved in implementation. Such an approach will help young professionals translate their knowledge into effective interventions.

Given your experience in establishing academic programmes in India and the US, what lessons can Indian universities draw from global models to strengthen design education while remaining rooted in local contexts?

Globally, design education has evolved via several pedagogical models, such as the Bauhaus, Ulm, Stanford d.school and Scandinavian approaches with globally lasting influences. These models offer important principles helpful to guide the development of the design discipline. While some emphasise the integration of art, craft and technology, others advance the understanding of design beyond aesthetics, establishing it as a rigorous, systematic discipline grounded in objective enquiry, empirical methods, iterative problem-solving and human-centred approaches, with a strong emphasis on social responsibility and long-term sustainability.

Many of these principles have shaped Indian design education. The opportunity now is to build upon these foundations through a diligent approach that combines the strengths of globally tried frameworks with a deeper understanding of India's diverse social fabric, rich cultural heritage and topical environmental concerns.

The use of clever design as a practical problem-solving tool is deeply ingrained in our cultural and social practices. Rather than simply replicating international models, Indian universities need to adapt their strengths to local conditions, drawing upon India's impressive regional and cultural diversity and century-old Indigenous Knowledge Systems. Such an approach will help develop educational models that are globally oriented but firmly grounded in Indian realities.

How can universities encourage research that connects architecture, urban planning, public policy and social equity, particularly in the context of India's rapidly expanding cities?

Teaching, research and practice are not separate domains but interconnected aspects of knowledge creation and communication. However, they are often perceived as distinct, leading to major gaps in delivery and educational experience. A strong academe-research-practice environment that brings together architects, urban planners, policymakers, social scientists and community stakeholders will enhance student learning and equip future professionals with relevant tools to carry out meaningful change in the world.

With artificial intelligence increasingly influencing architecture, urban planning and design, how should design institutions prepare students to use emerging technologies without compromising critical thinking, creativity and ethical judgement?

Emergent AI and other digital technologies are changing how products, services, buildings and infrastructure are conceived, designed, built, managed and evaluated. Yet, these technologies depend on human judgement, contextual understanding and interdisciplinary thinking to respond meaningfully to people, places and purpose.

These technologies, just like a sharp knife, can be put to socially good or totally disastrous ends, depending on how they are used - like a surgeon, chef or a criminal. Therefore, design institutions need to prepare students to harness AI and other similar technologies thoughtfully, as powerful tools that can improve the quality of life through clever thinking and better design.

Design education therefore needs to place informed emphasis on technological proficiency, critical thinking, creativity and ethical responsibility. The objective should be to prepare ethically sound professionals who can critically evaluate technological outputs, recognise their limitations and employ emerging technologies responsibly to develop socially beneficial solutions.

As provost of Anant National University, how do you assess whether design education is translating into meaningful career opportunities and enabling graduates to address real-world challenges beyond the classroom?

As the old adage goes, “The proof of the pudding is in the eating.” At Anant, we assess the contribution of our design education through the professional journeys of our graduates and their impact in the real world.

An encouraging indicator is the diversity of pathways our graduates pursue across manufacturing, advanced services, technology, education and the social sector. Our alumni are contributing to leading organisations such as Piramal Finance, Reliance, Accenture, Titan, TVS, Maruti, TCS and Teach For India, reflecting the relevance of design capabilities across domains.

Entrepreneurship is another significant outcome. Over the past three years alone, six of our graduates have established start-ups with annual turnovers of up to Rs 1 crore each, spanning healthcare, women's health and hygiene, robotics and sustainable manufacturing.

Ultimately, meaningful design education goes beyond conventional placement outcomes. It prepares appropriately skilled professionals to apply their knowledge across diverse contexts, create new opportunities and contribute meaningfully to society.

data.title: Alkem Laboratories gets USFDA warning letter with OAI classification for Daman facility
data.description:
Alkem Laboratories Ltd. on Thursday, November 19, said the US drug regulator has issued official action indicated (OAI) to the company's manufacturing facility in Amaliya, Daman.

The company said the US Food and Drug Administration (USFDA) inspected the facility from April 20, 2026 to May 1, 2026 and issued the warning letter on November 18, 2026.

Alkem said the warning letter pertains to observations made by the USFDA during its inspection of the unit and requires the company to implement appropriate corrective and preventive actions to address the observations and prevent recurrence.

Alkem Labs said it will respond to the USFDA within the stipulated timeline. It added that it continues to manufacture and supply approved products from the facility to the US market.

The company added that there is no material impact on its current operation, financial or other activities of the company.

Alkem Laboratories reported its second quarter results earlier this month.

Its net profit declined 11.7% to ₹675.3 crore from ₹765 crore in the second quarter last year. Its revenue increased 13.8% to ₹4,552 crore from ₹4,001 crore last year.

The company's earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortization (EBITDA) increased 11.3% to ₹1,025 crore from ₹921 crore last year. Its EBITDA margin contracted by 50 basis points to 22.5% from 23% in the year-ago period.

Shares of Alkem Laboratories are trading 1.7% lower on Thursday at ₹5,133. The stock is down 6% so far this year.

data.title: Anandkumar Ramaraj Joins Barclays As Vice President – CFO Business Partner
data.description:
Ramaraj brings over 17 years of experience in business finance, financial planning and analysis, budgeting, forecasting and performance management

Barclays has appointed Anandkumar Ramaraj as Vice President – CFO Business Partner, according to an update shared by him on LinkedIn.

Ramaraj joins Barclays after working with Wells Fargo, where he served as Vice President – Business Finance Lead for Cards, Personal Loans, Retail Services and Auto Finance. He held the position from February 2026 to November 2026.

At Wells Fargo, he previously served as Senior AVP – Business Finance Lead for Cards, Merchant Services and Personal Loans from August 2024 to January 2026. Before that, he was Senior AVP – Finance Business Partner for Credit Cards from September 2022 to August 2024.

Ramaraj has over 17 years of experience in business finance and financial planning and analysis (FP&A). His professional experience includes business finance, budgeting, forecasting, performance management, financial modelling and business partnering.

Before joining Wells Fargo, he worked at Spice Money as Senior Manager from October 2021 to September 2022. He was associated with Jio Financial Services as Manager – Business Finance from March 2017 to October 2021, where he worked on zero-based budgeting for businesses including Payments Bank, payment gateway and insurance.

Earlier, he worked as Analyst III at BNY Mellon from August 2016 to March 2017.

Ramaraj holds an Executive Programme in Strategic Finance from the Indian Institute of Management, Lucknow, which he completed between February 2021 and January 2022. His LinkedIn profile also lists an association with Symbiosis Centre for Distance Learning.

data.title: JAKSON Green To Acquire Majority Stake In Ocior Energy
data.description:
The deal brings renewable energy, green hydrogen and ammonia capabilities under one platform, with projects spanning India and international markets

JAKSON Green has signed definitive agreements to acquire a majority stake in Ocior Energy India, in a move to expand its clean energy portfolio across renewable power and green fuels. The transaction will combine JAKSON Green’s capabilities in renewable energy, independent power production, engineering, procurement and construction (EPC), and operations and maintenance (O&M) with Ocior Energy’s expertise in green hydrogen, green ammonia, green methanol and Power-to-X projects.

The companies expect the partnership to accelerate project development and strengthen their presence across the green molecules value chain. Financial details of the transaction, including the acquisition value and the precise stake to be acquired, were not disclosed in the announcement.

Expanding Clean Energy Portfolio

The acquisition will bring Ocior Energy’s green fuel projects into JAKSON Green’s broader clean energy platform. The combined capabilities are expected to support the development of projects across India, the Middle East and North Africa.

Green hydrogen and its derivatives, including green ammonia and green methanol, are emerging as potential alternatives to fossil fuels in sectors seeking to reduce emissions. The acquisition could help JAKSON Green expand beyond renewable power generation and project execution into the production and supply of these fuels.

Green Ammonia Projects

Ocior Energy’s portfolio includes 85,000 metric tonnes per annum (MTPA) of green ammonia supply awarded by the Solar Energy Corporation of India (SECI) under an initial 10-year offtake agreement.

The company is also developing a green ammonia plant with a planned capacity of 200,000 MTPA in Gopalpur, Odisha. These projects add to its presence in the emerging green ammonia market, where long-term offtake arrangements can provide greater visibility on future demand.

Hydrogen Projects Under Development

Ocior Energy’s portfolio also includes two green hydrogen projects, each with a capacity of 5 kilotonnes per annum (KTPA). The projects are being developed for Bharat Petroleum Corporation (BPCL) in Madhya Pradesh and Hindustan Petroleum Corporation (HPCL) in Visakhapatnam.

The projects broaden the partnership’s exposure to green hydrogen production and industrial applications, alongside its ammonia development pipeline.

Global Expansion Plans

With a growing project pipeline across India, the Middle East and North Africa, the partnership aims to expand JAKSON Green’s international presence and accelerate the development of clean energy projects.

The acquisition’s eventual impact will depend on project execution, financing requirements, demand for green fuels and the ability to bring projects into commercial operation. The companies have not disclosed the transaction value or a completion timeline.

data.title: Cilicant Appoints Anil Acharya As Chief Financial Officer
data.description:
Acharya moves to Cilicant from Otis Elevator Company, where he most recently served as Regional Finance Head – West and Infrastructure Business

Cilicant has appointed Anil Acharya as its Chief Financial Officer (CFO), according to an announcement shared by the company on LinkedIn.

Acharya is a Chartered Accountant and Company Secretary with an MBA. He has experience in finance leadership across the manufacturing and industrial sectors.

Before joining Cilicant, Acharya was associated with Otis Elevator Company, where he most recently served as Regional Finance Head – West and Infrastructure Business. He held the position from December 2024 and was responsible for overseeing finance operations for a portfolio valued at $140 million, leading an 11-member team and reporting directly to the CFO.

He previously served as Regional Finance Head – West at Otis Elevator Company from February 2022 to November 2024. Before that, he held the position of Senior Manager – Finance between April 2019 and February 2022 and Manager – Finance from November 2016 to March 2019.

Earlier in his career, Acharya worked as Manager – Business Finance at Tata Motors from January 2015 to November 2016. He was also associated with KEC International as Assistant Manager – Finance and Accounts (FPNA) between August 2012 and January 2015.

His earlier professional experience includes working as Audit Manager at Khandelwal Jain & Co. from November 2010 to August 2012 and as an Auditor at Shambhu Gupta and Co. from September 2006 to October 2010.

Acharya completed his Chartered Accountancy qualification from the Institute of Chartered Accountants of India (ICAI) between 2005 and 2010. He also holds a Company Secretary qualification from the Institute of Company Secretaries of India (ICSI), which he pursued between 2007 and 2010.

In his professional profile, Acharya lists experience in accounts, financial controlling and taxation, along with financial procedures, budgeting, variance reporting, cost modelling, product costing and cost management.

data.title: TCS Eyes Bosch Acquisition To Expand Engineering Revenue Base
data.description:
The proposed acquisition could involve up to 3,000 employees and give TCS access to engineering talent and long-term service revenue

Tata Consultancy Services (TCS) is in early discussions to acquire part of Bosch’s technology and product development operations in India, in a potential transaction that could involve the transfer of up to 3,000 employees. The proposed deal could expand TCS’ engineering capabilities and contracted revenue base, while helping Bosch reduce costs, according to a Mint report published on 18 November.

The discussions remain preliminary, with board-level deliberations expected next month. The transaction’s valuation, the operations involved and the final employee transfer arrangements have not been disclosed.

Acquisition And Cost Strategy

For TCS, the potential acquisition could provide access to established engineering teams working on emerging technologies, including physical artificial intelligence (AI), which integrates AI into machines, robots and autonomous systems.

For Bosch, transferring some technology and product development activities could help contain operating costs. However, the financial implications for both companies will depend on the deal structure, employee costs and the commercial arrangements agreed between them.

Revenue Visibility And Margins

Acquisitions of captive technology centres can provide IT services companies with established teams and long-term service contracts, offering greater revenue visibility amid uncertain demand. However, employee transfers can also create initial margin pressure if the acquired workforce has higher salary costs than the buyer’s existing employees.

Sushovon Nayak, Lead IT Analyst at Anand Rathi Institutional Equities, told Mint that long-term service contracts can help IT firms secure revenue over several years. Whether the proposed Bosch transaction includes such an agreement remains unclear.

Bosch’s India Operations

Bosch established its Indian technology operations in Bengaluru in 1997 through Bosch Global Software Technologies (BGSW), subsequently expanding to Hyderabad, Pune and Coimbatore.

According to the report, India accounts for approximately four-fifths of Bosch’s global capability centre workforce of 28,900 employees, with Bengaluru accounting for around half of the employees. The precise operations and workforce that could move to TCS have not been established.

The potential transaction concerns Bosch’s technology and product development operations and is separate from Bosch Ltd., the listed Indian automotive components manufacturer.

TCS Expands Acquisition Strategy

The proposed deal follows TCS’ recent acquisitions and technology partnerships aimed at expanding its capabilities and strengthening client relationships.

In October, TCS acquired Best Buy’s India technology centre. In August, it acquired Porsche’s management and IT consulting arm, MHP, for USD 373 million. TCS also secured a five-year Porsche IT modernisation contract valued at USD 1.45 billion.

The Bosch discussions remain at an exploratory stage. The purchase price, profitability of the operations and any long-term service commitments will determine the transaction’s financial value for TCS, while the final structure will shape the potential cost benefits for Bosch.

data.title: BABA Stock Dips Further After Hitting 22-Month Low — US AI Curbs Weigh Ahead Of Earnings, But Retail Bulls Aren’t Budging
data.description:
Key points:
  • Analysts expect Q2 revenue to grow 9% to $40.49 billion and adjusted profit to rise over 150% to $1.65 per share.
  • BABA tumbled to a 22-month low on Wednesday as investors assessed how new U.S. limits on access to advanced AI technology would affect its business.
  • Retail sentiment for BABA was ‘extremely bullish.’

Alibaba Group Holding (BABA) stock dipped over 2% in overnight trading ahead of Thursday’s session, nearing a two-year low and signaling a bearish setup ahead of the Chinese tech giant’s quarterly report.

BABA tumbled to a 22-month low the previous day as investors assessed how new U.S. limits on access to advanced AI technology would affect its business.

Earlier this week, the U.S. announced rules restricting overseas data centers from remotely providing large amounts of advanced U.S. chip computing to companies in China and other restricted countries.

The rules also add licensing requirements for certain chip sales to Indonesia, Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand and Brazil. On Wednesday, Reuters reported that the government is considering asking U.S. companies to publicly disclose when they use Chinese AI models, potentially on their websites.

Meanwhile, Alibaba is also under authorities’ scrutiny over its link to Megaspeed and its former CEO, Alice Huang, who are said to have ties to Beijing and are at the center of the recent crisis at Nvidia.

BABA Results On The Deck

Analysts expect fiscal second-quarter revenue to grow 9% to $40.49 billion and adjusted profit to rise over 150% to $1.65 per share, according to Koyfin.

Once riding the AI wave, Alibaba has plunged in recent months as investors worry that heavy AI spending and price competition in e-commerce are squeezing profits and cash flow, with a weak outlook for the Chinese economy further dampening sentiment. BABA is down by over 42% year to date.

Retail View On BABA

On Stocktwits, the retail sentiment for BABA has risen sharply over the past week and was ‘extremely bullish’ as of early Thursday.

“$BABA time (to) start loading after earnings. Will be good in 5 years,” said a trader, while another called the stock “way undervalued.”

A third wrote: “this company that makes multiple billions of dollars and invested in themselves goes down every day. The bleeding has to stop at a certain point. It’s not going to zero, so where’s it gonna end? Who knows, but the turnaround is gonna be epic and I’m gonna dump another half million dollars into this.”

data.title: Deutsche Telekom's Tech Fund Invests $110 Million in Mistral AI
data.description:
By Dominic Chopping

Deutsche Telekom's technology investment fund has invested around $110 million in Mistral AI as part of the French artificial-intelligence startup's Series D funding round.

The AI company completed its latest financing in September, raising a total of 3 billion euros ($3.29 billion) and lifting its valuation above 21 billion euros with backing from existing investors like Samsung Electronics and ASML Holding as well as new investors such as Advent, funds and accounts managed by BlackRock and the Grand Duchy of Luxembourg.

The round was co-led by Samsung, EQT-managed Scaleup Europe Fund and existing investor PSG Equity.

Deutsche Telekom said Thursday that its T.Capital Tech Fund invested 100 million euros in the round, paving the way for a strategic partnership to bring European artificial intelligence to German enterprises and public institutions.

"The investment marks a first step towards combining Deutsche Telekom's sovereign infrastructure, customer relationships and integration expertise with Mistral's frontier models, enterprise software and deployment capabilities as part of a future strategic partnership," the German company said in a statement.

The companies plan to support German businesses and public institutions to adopt AI, particularly in industrial and regulated sectors, it added.

Mistral AI in September opened a research and operational hub in Munich to advance Industrial AI for European manufacturing and heavy industry.

"We built Mistral so that European enterprises can deploy frontier AI they fully control, on their own data, in their own infrastructure," said Mistral AI Chief Financial Officer Johan Bergqvist. "T.Capital's investment is a strong signal: together, DT and Mistral can bring sovereign, trustworthy AI to German industry and public institutions at scale."

Write to Dominic Chopping at dominic.chopping@wsj.com

data.title: Netease Inc. Profit Drops In Q3
data.description:
BEIJING (dpa-AFX) - Netease Inc. (NTES) announced earnings for third quarter that Drops, from the same period last year

The company's bottom line totaled RMB8.402 billion, or RMB13.03 per share. This compares with RMB8.616 billion, or RMB13.36 per share, last year.

Excluding items, Netease Inc. reported adjusted earnings of RMB9.164 billion or RMB14.21 per share for the period.

data.title: REG - Elenia Verkko Oyj - Fixed-term one-time rebate on distribution fees
data.description:
RNS Number : 8650D Elenia Verkko Oyj 19 November 2026  

Fixed-term one-time rebate on network distribution fees

In connection with its routine end-of-regulatory-period review, the Energy Authority (the “EA”) released a decision on 28 May 2025 determining that in their interpretation Elenia Verkko Oyj (“Elenia”) has applied incorrect accounting in the notes (differentiated accounts) to the financial statements since the beginning of the previous regulatory period in 2020 (the “Decision”). These items were created in connection with Elenia’s sale of its district heating business in 2019 and Elenia group’s corporate reorganisation in 2020. The EA required Elenia to change the accounting treatment of these items, which is expected to adversely impact Elenia’s historical regulatory asset base and allowed rate of return and, in turn, reduce the level of regulated revenue Elenia is permitted to earn. As a result of this unexpected Decision, Elenia’s regulatory position at the end of the previous regulatory period ending in 2023, is expected to turn from an under recovery of allowed regulatory return (deficit) to an over recovery of allowed regulatory return (surplus). Elenia has appealed the Decision to the Market Court, as to whether the items in question relate to the regulated electricity distribution business, with a verdict expected in the second half of 2027, which may be further appealed to the Supreme Administrative Court.

As a result of the Decision, Elenia’s regulatory position is expected to be in surplus for two consecutive regulatory periods (including the current regulatory period ending in 2027), which is not allowed and bears the risk of a penalty under the Finnish regulation. To mitigate the potential risk of two consecutive periods being in surplus, Elenia has decided to proceed with a one-time rebate, adjusting its revenue for 2027 so that its regulatory position is in deficit at the end of the current regulatory period.

Against that backdrop, in 2027 Elenia intends to provide all its customers in one or more instalments with the one-time rebate on its network distribution fees. The rebate is expected to amount in aggregate to 50-75% of annual Group EBITDA. Elenia has sufficient liquidity available to cover the resulting shortfall in revenue and cash flow.

In line with the Common Terms Agreement originally dated 10 December 2013, as amended (the “CTA”), the rebate will be treated as an exceptional and non-recurring item for the purposes of the covenant calculations. Elenia has proactively engaged with its auditor and rating agencies, and it does not expect the rebate to have rating implications. Elenia expects to remain in full compliance with the CTA and other obligations notwithstanding the fixed-term rebate. Elenia will keep its stakeholders appraised of any further relevant developments regarding the implementation of the one-time rebate and the outcome of the related court case.

data.title: Twilio Powers Chelsea FC to Cut Campaign Launch Times from 48 Hours to Under 15 Minutes
data.description:
Twilio (), the infrastructure for customer engagement in the AI era, kicked off its SIGNAL World Tour London, by unveiling that Chelsea Football Club has slashed campaign launch times from 48 hours to under 15 minutes with Twilio Segment.

Building a Single View of the Global Fan

Chelsea’s global fans interact with the Club across matchdays, ticketing, its mobile app, ecommerce and other digital experiences. Historically, these interactions sat across siloed systems, creating duplicate customer records for a single fan. By consolidating its data, Chelsea removed over 460,000 duplicate records. With this cleaner and unified fan database, campaign launch time has been reduced from 48+ hours to under 15 minutes.

Beyond the Pitch: Elevating the Fan Experience

Chelsea is now able to send its fans highly relevant messages tailored to them right as the action happens on the pitch. With Twilio Segment, Chelsea is able to:

  • Create Real-Time Offers: After Estêvão Willian’s extraordinary goal during the 3-0 victory vs Barcelona in November 2025, Chelsea used Twilio Segment to identify fans who had selected Estêvão as their favourite player during mobile app onboarding. Chelsea triggered a real-time, personalised "Blue Friday" email offer, driving a 60% increase in conversion rates compared to standard seasonal benchmarks.

  • Predict Fan Purchases: To support the restock of the sold-out 2025/26 Third Kit, Chelsea leveraged Twilio Segment’s Predictive Audiences, which analysed historical purchasing behaviour and made predictions of which fans were most likely to buy. This data informed a Meta-sponsored ads campaign, generating a 16% click-rate uplift over standard campaigns and delivering a five-figure incremental revenue gain.

  • Use data-driven approaches for paid marketing: During the 2025/26 season, Chelsea continued to use Segment’s Predictive models to inform its paid media strategy. Chelsea saw an increased paid media return on ad spend of 22% and paid media revenue rose 75%, year-on-year.

Phil Lynch, Chief Digital Officer for Chelsea Football Club, said: “Our supporters don’t experience Chelsea through a single channel. They might be at Stamford Bridge, following a match from another country, using our app or interacting with Chelsea online. Our ambition is to connect those experiences so we can better understand what matters to individual supporters and make every interaction with Chelsea more relevant to the fan. Working with Twilio is helping us turn those different touchpoints into a more connected relationship with our fans across the world.”

Peter Bell, Vice President of EMEA Marketing at Twilio, said: “Marketing needs to be personal. When you have the right context, you can drive fan interaction. By shifting from legacy data silos to Twilio's context rich architecture, Chelsea has eliminated the lag between a real-world match event and commercial activation. Being able to capture fan demand at the moment of 'peak emotion', and launching campaigns in under 15 minutes instead of 48+ hours, is exactly how modern brands should drive sustainable ROI. With Twilio, Chelsea is demonstrating what engagement looks like at scale, with measurable results for the organisation.”

Chelsea plans to build on the programme during the 2026/27 season by developing targeted propensity and customer lifetime value predictive models, as well as by integrating systems more broadly within the Club. Following the success of early integrations, Chelsea is advancing towards additional real-time matchday interactions, with examples including special offers being triggered the moment a fan scans their ticket at the physical turnstile. By merging real-world movements with digital marketing, Chelsea and Twilio will continue to make the fan experience seamless and highly relevant.

data.title: Nearly all euro zone banks are struggling with tech risks, ECB says
data.description:
Almost all major euro zone lenders are showing deficiencies in how they manage their cybersecurity, the European Central Bank said on Thursday, adding that supervisors will zoom in on AI-enabled attacks in the next two years.

  • In its annual report on the state of the euro zone banking system, the ECB said 96% of the large banks on its watch received mediocre or poor ratings for their ability to manage operational and IT risks

  • This reflected outdated systems, weak operational controls and growing dependence on external technology providers

  • Asset managers, custodians, universal banks and investment banks received some of the weakest assessments. Even globally systemic lenders continued to struggle

  • Elsewhere in the report, the ECB said its overall core capital requirement for the sector stood at 11.3% of risk-weighted assets for 2027, roughly stable from 11.2% in 2026

  • The ECB applied additional leverage ratio requirements to 14 banks to stop them from taking on too much risk. It also set non-binding "guidance" for five banks in order to strengthen their resilience under stress

  • In 2026, the ECB imposed new "qualitative" measures on 78 banks, requiring changes to governance, controls and risk management processes rather than additional capital or liquidity

  • The measures focused on weaknesses in bad-loan management, board effectiveness, and banks' ability to aggregate data and produce reliable risk reports

  • The ECB's first priority for 2027-29 will be prudent credit underwriting standards and risk-based loan pricing

data.title: Brazil's corn ethanol boom accelerating growth of feedlot beef
data.description:
Key points:
  • Brazil's corn ethanol industry produces millions of tons of animal feed
  • Animal feed output and feedlot production have grown side-by-side since 2017
  • Cattle ranchers are seeking sites near corn ethanol plants

By Oliver Griffin

Brazil's booming corn ethanol plants are producing record amounts of animal feed products as part of their refining process, helping drive a surge in feedlot cattle in the world's largest beef producer and heralding more dramatic expansion ahead.

Brazil, long a sugarcane ethanol powerhouse, has seen corn ethanol output grow from practically nothing to more than a quarter of its total ethanol production over the last decade thanks to massive expansion of the country's corn crop, according to industry figures.

That has resulted in the production of millions of tons of dried distillers grains with or without solubles (DDG/S), a high-protein animal feed. DDG/S is left after corn starch is fermented and turned into ethanol, concentrating the content of protein and other nutrients in the kernels.

The grains have found a welcome market among ranchers across Brazil, pushing ever more cattle into feedlots and helping drive the biofuel's profitability, with dozens more plants in the pipeline.

The combination benefits both sectors, which are among the largest industries in Brazil. Domestic demand for ethanol is driven by a current government-mandated blend of 32% ethanol in gasoline, while demand from importers such as China for young beef necessitates more intense rearing cycles using nutrient-dense feed like DDG/S.

DDG/S offers "a spectacular opportunity for feedlot operations," said Mauricio Velloso, president of national feedlot association ASSOCON. "It's such a clear facilitator that it's encouraging new livestock producers to enter the feedlot business, precisely because of how easy it makes managing the diet."

MORE FEED, MORE FEEDLOTS

Since corn ethanol maker FS inaugurated Brazil's first corn-ethanol plant during the 2017-2018 season, Brazilian production of DDG/S has rocketed from 280,000 metric tons to more than 4.8 million tons in the 2025-2026 season, according to data from corn ethanol industry body UNEM.

"The industry is in unrestrained expansion," said Andrea Verissimo, UNEM's director of international relations and communications, adding that output of animal feed co-products in the 2026-2027 season is expected to hit 5.71 million tons.

Brazilian feedlot production reached 4.9 million head of cattle in 2017 and has set a new record every year since then, hitting 9.25 million cattle in 2025, according to a census by animal nutrient producer DSM-Firmenich . The company forecast in June that a new record of 9.78 million feedlot cattle will be slaughtered this year.

In 2025, feedlot cattle accounted for 22% of animals slaughtered in Brazil, up from close to 16% in 2017, according to Reuters calculations comparing DSM-Firmenich's feedlot census with data from government statistics agency IBGE.

"The expansion of the corn-ethanol industry — and, consequently, the greater availability of co-products like DDG/S — has contributed to the development of feedlot operations in Mato Grosso," said Ana Eufrazio, a cattle farming analyst at researcher IMEA, referring to Brazil's top beef-producing state on the southern edge of the Amazon rainforest.

From 2005 to 2025, Mato Grosso's pasture space shrank from 25.6 million hectares (63.3 million acres) to 16.9 million hectares as production more than tripled to over 118 kilograms per hectare, Eufrazio said, adding that more intense cattle rearing allows for increased output from smaller areas of land.

Growth of feedlot operations also depends on market conditions, including input costs, Eufrazio said.

Corn ethanol cannot take all the credit for the boom, some industry participants said.

"I still view the broader, structural factors — such as the advancement of agriculture — as the primary drivers behind the growth of feedlot operations," said Walter Patrizi, DSM-Firmenich's feedlot manager for Latin America.

CORN ETHANOL INDUSTRY GROWTH SURGING

Beef producers are looking to build feedlots close to corn ethanol plants, Verissimo and Velloso said, as ranchers try to take advantage of wet distillers grains — or WDG — a related animal-feed product with a shorter shelf life but nutritional benefits and lower production costs.

Producer FS has seen increased consumption of its animal feed products and growing numbers of feedlots in proximity to its three operating plants, said Victor Trenti, the company's commercial director.

The margin of animal feed and other co-products can represent around 25% of total revenue at corn ethanol plants, according to the US Department of Agriculture, helping establish lower breakeven production costs relative to sugarcane ethanol plants.

DDG/S is among a number of products that brought breakeven production costs for corn ethanol at a plant in Mato Grosso to 1.84 reais (around $0.31) per liter in July, according to the USDA, compared to 2.22 to 2.36 reais per liter for sugarcane ethanol produced in Brazil's center-south region in the same month.

DDG/S typically trades at a 10% to 20% premium to the price of corn, Trenti said, adding that farmers pay more for nutritional gains and to avoid grinding their own grains.

FS produces around 2 million tons of DDG/S per year, which could rise to around 3 million tons as two new plants come online soon, said Trenti.

Currently, 29 corn ethanol plants are operating in Brazil while 27 are under construction or in planning stages, according to UNEM.

"In five years, we expect (DDG/S production) to double, reaching 12 million tons per year here in Brazil," Trenti said.

data.title: European TTF Gas Rebounds on Colder Weather, Low Storage — Market Talk
data.description: European natural-gas prices rise in early trading following the previous session's drop, with the benchmark Dutch TTF contract now up 3.7% to 83.80 euros a megawatt hour. According to ANZ analysts, the recent decline was driven by increased LNG shipments from the U.S. and weaker demand from some major Asian importers, which allowed more cargoes to be redirected toward European markets. However, weather forecasts point to colder temperatures ahead, potentially boosting heating demand and increasing pressure on supplies. Meanwhile, European gas storage levels remain relatively low, standing at 69.9% full, compared with approximately 81.9% last year, leaving the region more vulnerable to increased demand during the winter months. (giulia.petroni@wsj.com)

data.title: EDAN Presents Integrated Medical Innovations at MEDICA 2026, Strengthening Global Healthcare Connections
data.description:
Edan Instruments, Inc. (300206. SZ), a global provider of medical devices and healthcare solutions, is presenting its latest innovations at MEDICA 2026, taking place November 16–19 in Düsseldorf. The event provides an important platform for industry exchange and an opportunity for EDAN to engage with European partners on evolving healthcare needs.

This press release features multimedia. View the full release here: https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20261118813326/en/

“Germany and Europe are important partners in the global healthcare industry. As China’s medical technology sector expands internationally, closer collaboration with European healthcare professionals and industry partners can create opportunities for shared progress,” said Alex You, Senior Director of Marketing, Customer Service, Global Connectivity & Integration at EDAN. “By understanding local clinical needs and translating them into accessible, reliable solutions, we can contribute to more effective healthcare. MEDICA offers a valuable opportunity to strengthen these connections and exchange perspectives.”

Making its debut, the Acclarix LX9S is powered by the SynSight zone sonography platform, delivering consistent image clarity across diverse clinical scenarios. It features a new eSRI imaging algorithm, alongside a 23.8-inch display, optical trackball, and redesigned touchscreen interface. These upgrades enhance imaging performance, streamline workflows, and support confident diagnostic decision-making.

In Patient Monitoring, EDAN highlighted the iV100, which functions both as a transport monitor and as a multi-parameter module within the iV Series. With real-time PresCCO continuous cardiac output, advanced parameters, and clinical assistive applications, the iV Series supports precise and efficient critical care across varied clinical environments.

In cardiology, Smart ECG Web connects ECG devices across departments and healthcare facilities through a centralized platform for ECG data management, review, and reporting, supporting more connected clinical workflows. EDAN is also preparing to introduce a wearable Patch Holter for up to 14 days of continuous ECG recording, helping capture intermittent cardiac events that may not be detected during routine examinations.

EDAN’s OBGYN portfolio covers fetal and maternal monitoring, intrapartum imaging, endoscopy, colposcopy, and pelvic floor rehabilitation, supporting care across a range of obstetric and gynecologic settings.

In IVD, EDAN i500 blood gas and chemistry analyzer combines full benchtop capabilities with a compact design. Its latest upgrade features a co-oximetry panel and auto-QC functionality, making it well suited to critical-care settings. The H90 Series 6-part auto hematology analyzer, featuring RET detection, further expands EDAN’s testing capabilities.

In animal health, the CC30 Vet biochemistry analysis system focuses on assessing liver and kidney function in pets, with a range of cartridges and testing parameters to support different screening needs in veterinary practice.

Across its diverse medical portfolios, EDAN continues to turn clinical insights into practical solutions, with a focus on addressing real healthcare needs and improving the human condition.

For more information, please visit www.edan.com.
